title: Housebound and Aid-and-Attendance Rates on a DIC Award
content:
**Applies to:** Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) awards held by surviving spouses.

**Rule.** A housebound or aid-and-attendance rate category is granted on medical evidence showing the spouse is permanently housebound or needs the regular aid and attendance of another person; a spouse meeting both standards is paid only the aid-and-attendance addition. The higher rate is paid from the month after its effective date.

**Rate categories involved.** A grant of housebound status places the award in DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound) or DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision); a grant of aid-and-attendance status places it in DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance) or DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision). The rate category also changes when housebound or aid-and-attendance status ends.

### What the medical evidence shows — and the category granted

| Medical evidence shows the spouse is permanently housebound | Medical evidence shows the spouse needs the regular aid and attendance of another person | Granted | Addition paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | Housebound rate category | Housebound addition |
| No | Yes | Aid-and-attendance rate category | Aid-and-attendance addition |
| Yes | Yes | Aid-and-attendance rate category | Aid-and-attendance addition only |

### When the higher rate is first paid

The higher rate starts with the month after the month containing its effective date.

| Effective date of the higher rate (hypothetical) | First month paid at the higher rate |
|---|---|
| March 1 | April |
| March 31 | April |
| December 15 | January of the following year |

### Basis questions

**Does the spouse's own description of needing help decide the category?** The category is granted on medical evidence showing the standard is met.

**Is a spouse who is both housebound and in need of aid and attendance paid both additions?** No. Such a spouse is paid only the aid-and-attendance addition.
